author: Whitney Thomas
title: Conway women speak out about harassment by man without arms - NewsBreak
text:
By Whitney Thomas ,
1 hours ago CONWAY, Ark. – Many Conway women said they are uncomfortable visiting local parks and trails because of one man who has allegedly been preying on them for the last four years.
Andrea Andrews has been advocating for women about this since 2021.
“If someone is at a walking trail here in town, he’ll follow them from beginning to end while they’re there, and that’s scary as a woman alone,” Andrews said.
Conway police say man with no arms harassing women by asking to touch their feet Police were first alerted about Brian Reams in 2021. Many of the women said that Reams, who has no arms, would ask them to hug him and to see their feet.
He would also make inappropriate comments and continue to follow them when he was ignored or rejected. For some, like Robyn White, the harassment escalated.
“He came up to my work every single day that I was there; he would get aggressive with me if I told him that I didn’t want to hang out with him,” White said.
White says the harassment began in 2022 when she was just 18 years old, working at Arkansas Pineapple Whip. She said she eventually had to change jobs.
“Then I started working at Walmart, the Jackson Hewitt, he started coming up there, there were multiple people that told me he’s been banned from Walmart for stalking women asking to touch their feet, touch their toes. He followed a girl into the bathroom,” White said.
Reams was eventually arrested in March of 2023, and he was taken into custody again in May of 2025. He was charged with stalking, harassment and criminal trespassing.
The arrest was thanks in part to Andrews, who helped get more than 30 women to come forward.
“I was reached out to by some law enforcement, and they wanted me to have the women who were posting anonymously in my group about this gentleman to file police reports so that they could actually take action,” Andrews said.
But after serving a four-month sentence, Reams was released from jail on Sept. 17. Even though he has been banned from Conway parks and trails, White says that he is already back doing all the same things as before.
“There’s no change here; they clearly don’t think that there’s an issue,” White said. “He might be mentally disabled, but it is very clear that he knows what he is doing, and he knows it’s wrong.”
